answer: LINE(2nd) tends to outperform LINE(1st) on social network classification because the task is usually driven more by a node’s neighborhood context than by whether two nodes are directly connected. LINE(1st) preserves first-order proximity, meaning it tries to keep embeddings of adjacent nodes close together, which mainly captures direct links. LINE(2nd) preserves second-order proximity, meaning nodes are embedded so that nodes with similar neighbors have similar representations, even if they are not directly linked. In social networks, nodes often belong to the same community, role, or interest group and therefore share many neighbors; this makes second-order proximity a stronger signal for classification than direct edge existence. So the better performance of LINE(2nd) suggests that, for this task and dataset, similarity in neighborhood structure is more informative than immediate pairwise adjacency, i.e., second-order proximity is more important than first-order proximity for predicting labels.
